risk_note: RV2 (orders/** with risk/**). Queue job names that platform/queue's validateSend accepts (^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)*$): the risk-scan chain's 'freeze-expiry' / 'daily-alerts' were rejected with invalid_name at seed, continuation and heal, so the queue never had a job (frozen_until never auto-lifted, daily alerts never sent); renamed freeze_expiry / daily_alerts. Orchestrator ruling D10-343 folded in the same defect in orders: SNAPSHOT_RETRY_JOB 'snapshot-retry' renamed snapshot_retry (the compensation scan was never enqueued). singletonKey prefixes unchanged (freeze-expiry: / daily-alerts: / snapshot-retry:, now explicit constants), log event names and changed_by unchanged; old-name jobs never existed, so no data migration. A repo-wide static scan rule test ([B1-03w#7]) checks every job name in apps/api/src. Frozen tests asserting the old names (risk freeze-expiry / freeze-expiry-heal, orders snapshot-retry / snapshot-wiring; 11 files) had their job-name literals changed in the author commit by a fresh independent Claude and checked change-only by another (couli-runs/B1-03w/frozen-rename-check.md, D10-327 / D10-343); 40 tests of those files judged as a whole are red_exempt (D10-344). Codex was unavailable until 10-30, so tests and reviews ran on fresh independent Claude contexts (approvals id 36). D10-384 (2026-10-27): the repo-wide job-name scan [B1-03w#7] also caught orders' manual sync (B1-09i, merged 10-25 after these rule tests were written): 'manual-window' and 'manual-order-nos' would be refused by validateSend, so the back-office manual sync could never have been enqueued; both renamed to 'manual_window' / 'manual_order_nos' in the same PR (the constants, the job header comment and the unit-test literal only; ledger #1702 adds the paths and the two renames, which hit no rule-test file). Whether these two names were ever enqueued in production was not checked: this lane has no access to production queues, and the queue runtime refuses such names before any row is written.
